subject: Re: Request to feature Finly case study — sensitivity check
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@finly.com>
Cc: Sam Choe <sam.choe@finly.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the great conversation last week. I put together a short draft case study based on the metrics you shared (latency improvements, cost reduction, and faster rollout time). Would Finly be open to a short customer spotlight on our site and a brief quote from you? We’d aim to publish a short-form page and a downloadable PDF.

Draft attached for review — happy to edit anything you want removed. If it looks fine, we can also schedule a quick 20-minute review call and a quote sign-off.

Attachments: [Attachment: Finly_case_study_draft_v2.docx (23 KB)]

Next steps I had in mind:
- You review the draft (I can make edits)
- Legal/PR sign-off at Finly if required
- Redwood to publish and share final assets with you

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the draft and for the thoughtful write-up. We’re generally supportive of being a reference, but I need to flag one concern: we had a retention/config incident in January related to a misapplied caching policy that impacted two customers for ~6 hours. Our legal and ops teams asked us to be cautious about public statements that could imply zero-risk or suggest the event never happened.

Before signing off we need to:
- Confirm the case study language doesn’t downplay that incident
- Run your redacted incident postmortem by our legal team

I’ll circle in our security lead (Sam) and our legal counsel. Can you pause publication until we’ve completed a quick sensitivity check? We’d like to see the postmortem or a redacted summary to confirm the timeline and remediation wording.

Thanks for understanding.

— Olivia
Director of Marketing, Finly
olivia.barnes@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:26:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask

Team — forwarding Finly’s note. They asked for a hold until legal/ops confirm. Can we get guidance on:
1) whether we have an appropriately redacted incident postmortem we can send?
2) does marketing pause publishing assets unilaterally or do we need a formal withdraw/pause approval?

Current plan: pause public posting until Finly signs off. Evelyn, can you prepare a redacted postmortem (no internals, no PII) and share a Jira/drive link? Vivek, if there are technical clarifications we should include in the write-up, please add. Rishi, this may touch deal optics — do you want to weigh in on messaging?

Thanks — I’d like a short internal response I can share back to Olivia within the day.

— Marissa

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask

Marissa —

Agree we should pause externally for now. Quick guidance:
- Pause publishing immediately (marketing may hold draft in staging).
- Provide a redacted incident postmortem that explains the timeline, impact, and remediation without sensitive internal logs. That should be sufficient for legal review at Finly in most cases.
- We should propose a short excerpt for the case study that acknowledges the incident in neutral terms (e.g., "a temporary caching misconfiguration in Jan 2026 affected a subset of requests; Redwood implemented X remediation and monitoring changes"). Let Finly approve wording.
- Ask finance/sales if there are any contract/clause implications (credits given earlier?) — if there were credits or SLA concessions, confirm with me before publishing.

Evelyn/Vivek — can you prepare the redacted postmortem and a 2-3 sentence recommended public note? I’ll be available if Finly escalates.

— Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask

Hi —

Attached is a redacted postmortem and a suggested neutral excerpt for the public case study. Key points included:
- Summary of incident (Jan 12 2026): misapplied caching policy; four customers affected for ~6 hours.
- Root cause: config rollout gap + missing guardrail during a specific orchestration job.
- Remediation: immediate rollback, patch to rollout orchestration, additional monitoring and alerting, mandatory rollout checklist.
- Customer impact and remediation steps: credits offered to affected customers; proactive outreach done.

Suggested public sentence (for Finly approval):
"In January 2026, Finly and Redwood worked together to resolve a temporary caching configuration issue that impacted a subset of requests; Redwood implemented configuration guardrails and enhanced monitoring to prevent recurrence."

Attachments: [Attachment: incident_postmortem_redacted.pdf (48 KB)]

I recommend we hold publication until Finly gives explicit sign-off on this redacted doc and the suggested sentence. Happy to make edits per their legal team.

— Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@finly.com>, Sam Choe <sam.choe@finly.com>

Subject: Re: Customer spotlight: draft case study + quick publish ask — Pausing publication

Hi Olivia / Sam —

Thank you for raising this. Per Finly’s request, we will pause any public posting of the case study until you confirm in writing. Attached is a redacted postmortem and a single-sentence excerpt we propose for the public page. Please let us know whether:

1) Your legal team is comfortable with the attached redaction and the proposed wording, or
2) You’d like additional redaction or a different phrasing.

If we don’t hear back within two weeks we’ll follow up, but no assets will be published without Finly’s explicit approval.

Links:
- Draft case study (view-only): https://drive.google.com/finly-case-study-draft
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-20260112

Thanks again — we appreciate your partnership and want to ensure the final case study reflects your comfort level.

Best,

— Marissa Cole
